text:
incident-bot: ALERT: continuous-batching tail latency spike detected in us-west-2 (controller: cb-prod-1). error-rate 0.8% -> 3.4%, p95 token latency 520ms -> 2.1s, KV cache eviction rate x4. Paging on-call: @Alex (oncall) :rotating_light:

Alex (oncall): seeing the bot. I'm on it. grabbing dashboard now.

Sam (eng): timeline? did a config rollout go out?

Alex (oncall): checked deploys — no model changes in the last 2h, but there was a controller config push 10m ago (auto-batch controller flags).

Joy (infra): logs show KV cache object count climbing 3x since ~T-12m, GC not keeping up. microbatch size distribution skewed to 32 tokens in many requests.

Mike (runtime): continuous batching kernel is seeing huge inflight request fan-in at high concurrency. KV cache appears to get overloaded with many distinct prefixes, causing eviction thrash.

Alex (oncall): customer impact: some interactive endpoints degraded (webchat timeouts), internal SLOs: p95 breached on several routes. Not widespread 5xx but timeouts and slower responses.

Emily (sre): recommended mitigations: 1) temporarily reduce max_microbatch_size, 2) enable prefix jittering, 3) throttle controller admission for best-effort tier. Can we patch controller quickly?

Sam (eng): I can roll a hotfix to controller config. Proposed immediate changes: set max_microbatch_size=8 (from 32), enable jitter_ms=25, and set admission_shed_rate=0.2 for best-effort queue. Also enable KV soft-eviction safeguard: kv_cache.max_keys_threshold=0.75.

Alex (oncall): do it. Start with reducing microbatch size. We'll measure tail latency. Sam, deploy when ready, announce start/complete.

Sam (eng): applying patch now. command: 
```
kubectl set image deploy/controller controller=controller:v2.14-hotfix --namespace=cb-prod
kubectl patch cm cb-controller-config -p '{"data":{"max_microbatch_size":"8","jitter_ms":"25","admission_shed_rate":"0.2","kv_max_keys_threshold":"0.75"}}'
```

Sam (eng): patch applied, rolling restart started (pods 0/3 -> 3/3).

Joy (infra): routing note: shifting 15% of traffic to dedicated pool rd-dedicated-lowlat to reduce churn while we observe.

Mike (runtime): observing KV eviction rate dropping ~60% post-patch, microbatch histogram now showing mode at 6-8 tokens. p95 token latency falling.

Emily (sre): customer comms: prod webchat customers saw increased latency for ~20m, we mitigated; ops team to draft status update.

Alex (oncall): monitoring: set temporary alert thresholds to be more sensitive for next 1h. Also enable tracing on one problematic route to capture prefix diversity.

Sam (eng): added tracing flag for /v1/chat/generate for 10m window. collecting samples now.

incident-bot: NOTE: automatic rollback window ends in 30m. No rollback triggered.

Mike (runtime): found micro-pattern: a small set of upstream clients suddenly sent many long prompts causing large prefix branching; looks like a customer test hitting prod.

Emily (sre): action items: Sam - keep hotfix live for 45m then evaluate rollback; Joy - keep traffic shift until p95 < 600ms for 15m; Alex - prep handoff notes for night oncall.

Alex (oncall): Agreed. I'm going to do a formal handoff in 20m to @Sam who takes night coverage at 22:30 PST. After that, if condition persists, escalate to runtime lead @Mike.

Sam (eng): copying runbook steps into thread: 
1) if p95 > 1s => reduce max_microbatch_size to 4
2) if eviction_ratio > 0.5 => set admission_shed_rate=0.35 and ramp down best-effort to 5%
3) if error-rate > 5% => divert 30% traffic to rd-dedicated-lowlat and notify support

sre-runbook-bot: runbook linked: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/continuous-batching-kv-thrash

Alex (oncall): handing off to Sam at 22:30 PST. Current status: hotfix deployed, p95 back to ~480ms, eviction rate trending down, traffic shift in place. Will update if regressions occur.

Sam (eng): taking handoff. I'll keep the patch live and monitor traces. If we see reversion I'll follow runbook steps and open a priority PR for a more durable controller change.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, customer impact reduced. Incident remains open for monitoring.

Emily (sre): closing notes for now: root cause hypothesis - sudden high-diversity prefixes + large microbatches => KV cache blowup and eviction thrash. Mitigation effective: smaller microbatches + jitter + shed. Postmortem to be scheduled tomorrow. :memo:
